name: Niwa
tagline: A cozy idle garden that lives in your terminal and macOS menu bar and grows quietly while you work.
description: Niwa tucks a quiet stoneware tray of moss, bamboo, and bonsai into a corner of your terminal and macOS menu bar. There are no streaks to lose, no loud timers, and no notifications demanding attention while you think.

Built as a lightweight Rust TUI/CLI (niwa) paired with a native Swift menu bar companion, the garden reads gentle work cadence from active coding sessions—unfolding new shoots, blossoms, and evening lantern light at an unhurried pace.

features.title: Rust TUI & single-line CLI status
features.detail: Open a calm box-drawn courtyard in any split pane with niwa, or print a compact one-line botanical status for tmux and prompt bars.

features.title: Native Swift macOS menu bar companion
features.detail: Mirrors the same local garden state in the macOS menu bar with crisp monochrome glyphs and a popover courtyard card.

features.title: Zero-guilt idle growth
features.detail: Plants rest naturally when you step away instead of wilting—rewarding steady focus without gamified pressure or streak anxiety.

features.title: Shared local garden file
features.detail: Both the Rust TUI and Swift menu bar app read a tiny plain-JSON garden state on disk with near-zero CPU wakeups and zero network traffic.

install.label: CLI preview
install.note: In development — the Rust TUI/CLI binary (niwa) and Swift menu bar app will ship together in the first public beta.
